papers.title_en: When LLMs Develop Languages: Symbolic Communication for Efficient Multi-Agent Reasoning
papers.authors: Zhengqi Pei, Qingming Huang, Shuhui Wang
papers.evidence: 多智能体LLM系统自主发明符号语言进行高效通信和推理
papers.tldr: 大语言模型在推理时使用链式思维虽有效但产生大量冗余令牌，影响效率。CLSR框架使多个智能体各自发明并进化一套紧凑的符号语言（LSF），通过路由自适应选择单次调用、集成或组合来平衡准确率和令牌开销。实验表明，在复杂基准上，CLSR比标准CoT减少3-6倍令牌量，精度不降；理论分析还给出了令牌成本下界，显示多轮LSF协议可模拟程序执行。贡献在于提出了一种符号通信范式，使多智能体推理更高效。
papers.abstract_en: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) improves large language models (LLMs) on difficult reasoning tasks, but it often incurs long natural-language rationales that are poorly aligned with efficient machine reasoning. We propose Communicative Language Symbolism Routing (CLSR), a test-time framework in which multiple LLM agents autonomously invent, evolve, and share compact Language Symbolism Frameworks (LSFs), while a latent-free router adaptively selects and composes these languages per query to optimize the accuracy-token trade-off. Unlike prompt optimization that refines surface instructions, CLSR treats each LSF as a reusable symbolic protocol with compact symbols, usage rules, and a message-passing contract, and improves it through an evolutionary loop driven by correctness and token cost. At inference time, the router may invoke a single low-cost LSF call, ensemble multiple LSFs, or execute a multi-round LSF composition protocol on harder queries. Across challenging benchmarks, CLSR reduces latency-oriented generated token completion by $3\sim 6\times$ compared to standard CoT while maintaining accuracy. We further derive an information-theoretic lower bound on token cost under arbitrary symbolism and show that, under an interpreter-realizability premise, multi-round LSF protocols conditionally subsume program-execution pipelines. Code is publicly available (https://github.com/pzqpzq/LSF_MDia).

papers.title_en: Fourier-Diagonalized Natural Gradients and Sobolev Mirror Descent
papers.evidence: 用于PDE优化的傅里叶对角化自然梯度
papers.tldr: 自然梯度更新中，度量算子可被傅里叶变换对角化，并与Sobolev镜像下降共享谱域逆映射结构。Fisher度量具有正傅里叶符号，而Sobolev镜像几何对应Bessel势符号。两者符号一致时更新相同；否则Sobolev镜像下降作为谱预条件子。这为PDE和算子学习中的谱滤波与截断提供了逆度量几何视角，并提出了基于FFT的谱自然梯度实现。
papers.abstract_en: We study natural-gradient updates whose metric operators are diagonalized by the Fourier transform and relate them to Sobolev mirror descent. Translation-invariant Fisher geometries and Sobolev mirror geometries share a common inverse-map structure in the spectral domain. The Fisher metric is represented by a positive Fourier symbol, while Sobolev mirror geometry corresponds to the specific Bessel-potential symbol associated with the Sobolev norm. When these symbols coincide, the natural-gradient and mirror-descent updates are identical; otherwise, Sobolev mirror descent provides a canonical spectral preconditioner for the Fisher inverse geometry. This gives a mathematical lens through which spectral filtering and truncation techniques in PDE and operator learning can be viewed as natural actions of inverse metric geometry. We introduce Spectral Natural Gradient, an FFT-based implementation of these geometric updates.

papers.title_en: Atomic Task Graph: A Unified Framework for Agentic Planning and Execution
papers.authors: Yue Zhang, Sihan Chen, Ziwen Huang, Hanyun Cui, Kangye Ji, Zhi Wang
papers.evidence: 具有显式依赖图的统一智能体规划框架
papers.tldr: 针对现有LLM智能体依赖大模型或微调导致高成本与低泛化的问题，提出Atomic Task Graph (ATG)统一框架。ATG通过维护显式依赖图，在规划时递归分解任务形成有向无环图，执行时支持并行分支，错误时仅修复受影响区域。在三个交互基准上使用7B-8B模型，ATG在成功率和执行效率上均优于强基线。
papers.abstract_en: LLM-based agents have shown strong potential for solving complex multi-step tasks, yet existing performance improvements often rely on either scaling to larger backbone models or task-specific fine-tuning. The former incurs substantial computational costs, while the latter typically generalizes poorly across different tasks. Although prompt-based control is training-free and broadly applicable, existing methods still leave input-output dependencies between subtasks implicit in textual trajectories, making verified intermediate results difficult to reuse. To address these limitations, we propose Atomic Task Graph (ATG), a unified control framework for planning and execution. Specifically, ATG maintains an explicit graph to expose dependencies and support reuse. During planning, it recursively decomposes a high-level task into subtasks, forming a sequence of directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) whose evolution can be traced. During execution, the dependencies exposed by ATG allow independent branches to be executed in parallel, thereby improving execution efficiency. When failures are detected, ATG leverages the graph evolution history to localize the error source and repair only the affected region, preserving validated regions unchanged. Experiments show that ATG consistently outperforms strong baselines in success rate and execution efficiency across three interactive benchmarks using only 7B-8B backbones.
